CHIEF COMPLAINT
Difficulty with asthma during sports and mood concerns.

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a young athlete who reports worsening asthma symptoms that are interfering with water polo participation. Symptoms occur primarily with aerobic activity and include sensation of phlegm buildup in throat, cough, chest tightness, wheezing, and lightheadedness. Patient uses albuterol inhaler (2 puffs) for symptom relief, which helps with phlegm sensation but patient still requires sitting down to recover. Symptoms typically improve within 15 minutes of inhaler use. Patient reports experiencing tremor/shakiness after using albuterol, which was explained as a normal side effect. Symptoms occur with every aerobic workout and also triggered by exposure to smoke. No nighttime awakening from asthma symptoms. Currently using only rescue inhaler with no daily maintenance medication. Patient also reports mood concerns starting this year, describing significant stress related to SAT preparation and AP classes. Reports feeling down, lacking motivation, fatigue, and preferring to stay home rather than engage in social activities with friends. Denies difficulty with focus or information retention; primarily experiencing sadness and loss of motivation.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for seasonal allergies. Denies nighttime asthma symptoms. No other pertinent positives.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Asthma.

MEDICATIONS
Albuterol inhaler (2 puffs as needed).

ALLERGIES
Seasonal allergies noted.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient is a high school student involved in water polo. Currently studying for SATs and taking AP classes. Lives with friends nearby.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vital signs: Not documented.
General: Patient appears appropriately developed.
HEENT: Eyes normal. Ears show mild fluid bilaterally. Throat and tonsils normal.
Cardiovascular: Heart sounds normal.
Pulmonary: Lungs clear to auscultation bilaterally.
Abdomen: Bowel sounds normal, soft, non-tender, no masses palpated.
Neurologic: Reflexes normal and symmetric.

RESULTS
None documented.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Asthma, exercise-induced: Start montelukast (Singulair) daily as maintenance therapy given suspected allergic component and frequent exercise-triggered symptoms. Continue albuterol inhaler as needed for acute symptoms. Counsel on expected tremor side effect and to rest after inhaler use. Follow up in 6 weeks to assess response to therapy; patient should expect improvement within approximately 1 month.
2. Mood disorder/depressive symptoms: Patient reports new-onset sadness, anhedonia, and fatigue related to academic stress. Recommend starting therapy with a mental health professional. Will administer screening questionnaires. Follow up in 2 weeks to discuss results and therapy initiation.
